updates.title: The core 0.1.11: the skills /release and /release-prep always say the last released version, and the skill /start asks once whether to protect the branch main
updates.whatToDo: Copy the 5 files from the release. When your project has skills of its own, do not copy `docs/workflow/skills.md`: run `make skills-catalog`, which writes it again. The skills `/release` and `/release-prep` now say the last released version of the product wherever they name a version: in one line right after the product is chosen, in the draft, in the release ticket, in the pull request text and in the report. The skill `/start` has a new Part B: when the repository is on GitHub and has no ruleset, it asks once, "Protect the branch main now?". It asks only when the file `scripts/protect-main.sh` exists: the update `0.1.3-protect-main` brings that file.

updates.title: A script that protects the branch main on GitHub
updates.whatToDo: Copy the 2 files from the release. `scripts/protect-main.sh` creates one ruleset named `protect-main` on GitHub for the branch `main`: a pull request is required (with no approval), the check of `.github/workflows/check.yml` must pass, no force push, no deletion. It prints the rule and asks before it creates it. Nothing runs by itself: the skill `/start` of the update `0.1.3-core` asks once, "Protect the branch main now?", when the repository is on GitHub and has no ruleset. `scripts/sync-skills.sh` now also copies the new script.

updates.title: The command make protect-main, and the step that names it in the guides
updates.whatToDo: Take the update `0.1.3-protect-main` first: it brings `scripts/protect-main.sh`. Then, in `Makefile`: add `protect-main` to the list `.PHONY`, and add this target (the second line starts with a tab): `protect-main: ## Protect the branch main on GitHub: pull request and check required, no force push, no deletion (asks first; YES=1 asks nothing)` and `@bash scripts/protect-main.sh $(if $(YES),--yes)`. In `AGENTS.md`, add one line to the block "Commands": `make protect-main # on GitHub: protect the branch main (pull request and check required, no force push, no deletion); it asks first`. In `docs/start-a-new-monorepo.md`, add point 5 of step 10 from the release: run `make protect-main` right after the repository is on GitHub. Then run `make protect-main` once, when the repository is on GitHub and a person says yes.
